stem: The value of lim(x -> infinity) [(3x^2 - 2x + 1) / (5x^2 + x - 4)] is:

per_option_rationale.rationale: Divide numerator and denominator by x^2 (the highest power). Numerator: 3 - 2/x + 1/x^2. Denominator: 5 + 1/x - 4/x^2. As x -> infinity, all terms with 1/x or 1/x^2 go to 0. Limit = 3/5.

Dividing by x (linear term) instead of x^2, looking at the ratio of the x^1 coefficients (-2 in numerator and 1 in denominator) and reporting -2/1, instead of comparing the leading quadratic coefficients.

Using the constant terms (1 in numerator and -4 in denominator) as if they dominate at infinity, computing 1/(-4) and then reporting a positive version 1/4, ignoring that constant terms are dominated by quadratic terms.

Reasoning that both numerator and denominator grow to infinity as x -> infinity and concluding the ratio is also infinite, without recognising that both numerator and denominator are degree-2 polynomials so the ratio is finite.

explanation: For a rational function where numerator and denominator have the same degree, the limit at infinity is the ratio of leading coefficients; here 3/5.

explanation_sections.punchline: At infinity, only the leading terms survive; for equal-degree polynomials the limit is the ratio of leading coefficients.
explanation_sections.approach: State the property then contrast the confusable one. Both polynomials are degree 2. Divide by x^2: (3 - 2/x + 1/x^2)/(5 + 1/x - 4/x^2). As x->inf every 1/x and 1/x^2 term vanishes. Limit = 3/5. Contrast: comparing x^1 coefficients (wrong degree) gives -2/1; comparing constants (wrong degree) gives 1/(-4); seeing inf/inf and stopping gives 'infinity', but the ratio is bounded.
explanation_sections.lesson: For lim of P(x)/Q(x) as x->inf with deg(P)=deg(Q), the limit is always (leading coeff of P)/(leading coeff of Q).
explanation_sections.timing: About 70 seconds. Identify equal degrees (10 sec), read off leading coefficients (10 sec), write ratio (10 sec). Trap: using lower-degree coefficients.
